pick.headline: Romanian security forces fire on protesters in Timisoara
pick.summary: On December 17, 1989, Romanian army and Securitate forces opened fire on demonstrators in Timisoara, where protests had begun over the attempted eviction of the pastor Laszlo Tokes.
pick.significance: The massacre set off the revolution that overthrew Nicolae Ceausescu within a week.
pick.fbis: The East Europe Daily Report of December 18, 1989, carried Budapest Television's witness account of clashes in Timisoara after an attempt to evict Laszlo Toekes, with crowds shouting "Down with Ceausescu", and DIE WELT on his defenders.

alternates.headline: Red Brigades kidnap US General James Dozier
alternates.summary: On December 17, 1981, Red Brigades terrorists kidnapped US Army Brigadier General James Dozier, a NATO officer, from his flat in Verona.
alternates.significance: Dozier was the first American general kidnapped by European terrorists; Italian police rescued him unharmed on January 28, 1982.
alternates.fbis: The Middle East & Africa Daily Report of December 21, 1981, noted that Libya's JANA denied any role in the kidnapping of U.S. General James Dozier after an Italian paper reported U.S. officials did not rule it out.

evidence.title: FBIS Daily Report: Middle East & Africa, Vol. V No. 244, 21 December 1981

alternates.headline: Fernando Collor elected president of Brazil
alternates.summary: On December 17, 1989, Fernando Collor de Mello defeated Luiz Inacio Lula da Silva in Brazil's first direct presidential election since 1960.
alternates.significance: Collor's election completed Brazil's return to democracy; he was impeached three years later.
alternates.fbis: The Latin America Daily Report of December 20, 1989, carried Buenos Aires TELAM: President Menem sent warm congratulations to Fernando Collor de Mello on his election as Brazil's president.
